rename.from: ES6 import export compatibility with commonjs2

body:
Using `transform-es2015-modules-commonjs` results in the expected behavior. But that defeats the point of using native modules and webpack for tree shaking. Another thing I noticed is, webpack does not set `__esModule` flag on transpiled ES6 modules. This breaks functionality. See:
https://github.com/esnext/es6-module-transpiler/issues/86
https://github.com/Microsoft/TypeScript/issues/2719
https://github.com/markdalgleish/static-site-generator-webpack-plugin/issues/46#issuecomment-241088084

@bebraw I believe you should escalate the priority to something more important than "important" as this is absolutely critical to maintain consistency across different module formats and with other transpilers.

@sidjain26 I would like to you to confirm something for me as well. I believe we are coming across this via webpack@2.1.0-beta.21 and Angular RC6. Would you be please willing to downgrade to webpack@2.1.0-beta.19 and confirm that this is still a problem on this version? 

If it is not, (which is the behavior I am seeing) then we might be seeing the same bug.

@TheLarkInn I see the same behavior with `2.1.0-beta.19`. Made a repository to reproduce it at - https://github.com/sidjain26/webpack-bug. Do

```
npm start # in ./consume
```

In https://github.com/sidjain26/webpack-bug/blob/a24dc871f279dd373c227f5f5a8ceb1e0bd047b9/consume/main.build.js#L148

`__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__library_build_library_js__.__esModule` does not evaluate to be true, but I think it should.

Perhaps it should set the `__esModule` flag somewhere in here: https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/b0fffd50d35dd0eef734d189928c1ac4c5c9fb97/lib/dependencies/HarmonyExportExpressionDependency.js

Seems to be missing all the way from `2.0.0-beta` - https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/5f77afe5f4de24e7596838e689763b7f6fa2d6e1/lib/dependencies/HarmonyExportExpressionDependency.js

`babel-plugin-transform-es2015-modules-commonjs` sets the flag correctly - https://github.com/babel/babel/blob/71dff8c834191356bfc58d24f37e3601df96987e/packages/babel-plugin-transform-es2015-modules-commonjs/src/index.js#L11-L15

I'm really out of my depth here

issue.body:
**I'm submitting a bug report**

**Webpack version:**
`webpack@2.1.0-beta.21`

**Please tell us about your environment:**
OSX 10.x

**Current behavior:**
It appears that since @angular/core package has updated to RC6, there has been some reworking of how the packages are structure (ESM, etc.).

``` javascript
import {ViewEncapsulation} from '@angular/core';

console.log(ViewEncapsulation);
```

I receive the following errors in my console: 

![screen shot 2016-09-03 at 10 36 37 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3408176/18228907/5c8a1ec4-7227-11e6-848b-024541042499.png)

![screen shot 2016-09-03 at 10 36 40 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/3408176/18228903/44a3de12-7227-11e6-89d1-084f066d19f0.png)

**Expected/desired behavior:**
That there would be no error, and that `import`ing this exported member would not be undefined. 

This is critical for the AngularCLI to use with angular RC6. I'm cc'ing @robwormald who has also been trying to hunt down this issue. We have both been unsure if we missed a case for harmony namespace exports with named reexports underneath nested.

The named export mentioned is originally defined [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/%40angular/core/src/metadata/view.ts#L19-L43) and is then [rexported up a level here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/%40angular/core/src/core.ts#L14) which is then [namespaced reexported here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/%40angular/core/index.ts#L14). 

This was part of a major package overhaul by @mhevery in https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/979657989bab4fb93faf6a207d30760faa9bd696. 
### To Reproduce:
- `git clone https://github.com/TheLarkInn/webpack-developer-kit && cd webpack-developer-kit && git checkout experiment/show_beta_21_bug && npm install && npm run dev`
- Open browser and inspect console 
- See error there.
- **Interesting information: *
  This still appropriately works on downgrade to `webpack@2.1.0-beta.19` so I assume it is a change from there till .21.
- **Browser:** [all] 
- **Language:** [all|TypeScript|ES6/7|ES5]

body:
`__esModule = true` need to be set only on library export. It need to be set on the exports of the entry module. Inner modules don't need `__esModule`, it's just a babel hack.

Workaround:

`export const __esModule = true` in entry module.
Thank you for the work around. Will test.
@sokra Workaround fits in nicely for now, maybe this should be mentioned in the docs somewhere until it is fixed
